To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two-loop coefficient functions of the operator  G 2 in the large mass expansions of the correlators of two pseudoscalar and pseudovector currents are sizeable and can be important for the determination of the value for the corresponding condensates.

we have calculated in the two–loop approximation the coefficient functions of the operator $G^{2}$ in the large mass expansion of the two–point correlator of (pseudo) scalar currents and the two–point correlation function of (pseudo) vector operators.

the coefficient functions of the operator $G^{\mu \nu}$ in the large mass expansion of the two-point correlation functions of two pseudoscalar and two pseudovector currents are calculated in two-loop approximation and the obtained results are numerical sizeable and could play an important role in the determination of the value for the condensate $\langle G^{\mu \mu} \rangle$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large mass expansions in the correlators of currents of scalar, pseudoscalar and vector fields.
the calculation of the two-loop contributions to the large mass expansion of the correlator of two vector currents in QCD.
the calculation of the two-loop coefficient functions of the operator $G^2$ in the large mass expansion of the correlators of two pseudoscalar and pseudovector currents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the value of the condensate 〈G 2 〉, which is the only one of the condensates of dimension 6, that is not yet known, should be determined from the experimental data on the mass of the lightest pseudoscalar particle, and from the experimental data for the correlators of the two scalar currents.
the value of the coefficient function of the operator G2 is sizeable and that it could play an important role in the determination of the condensate 〈G2〉.
the value of the condensate is still uncertain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the large mass expansion is a very useful tool in the study of correlators of (pseudo) scalar currents.
, for the first time in QCD, two-loop coefficient functions of the large mass expansion for the correlators of two scalar currents, two vector currents, and two pseudoscalar currents are known.
the two-loop coefficient function of the operator G2 in the large-mass expansions of the correlator of two pseudoscalar currents has been calculated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the large mass expansion of the correlator of two (pseudo)-scalar currents can be reliably used to extract the value of the condensate 〈G 2〉.
, unlike for the scalar case, the coefficient function in the vector case is a complicated expression which cannot be written as a product of two simpler functions.
the two-loop coefficient function is negative for all the cases under consideration.
